title: Proto-cuneiform barley account of Kushim (MSVO 3, 29)
source: MS 1717 photograph, transliteration and English translation via CDLI (P005340)
description: Proto-cuneiform barley account of Kushim: a clay tablet from Uruk of about 3200-3000 BCE, among the earliest written documents, with CDLI's transliteration and English.
introduction:
This clay tablet (MS 1717, Schøyen Collection, Oslo, Norway) is a proto-cuneiform document of the Uruk III period, about 3200-3000 BCE, from Uruk. It is an account of barley over 37 months, closed with the sign group read KU ŠIM, often taken as the name or title of the official responsible (Kushim). The CDLI translation reads: '5617 1/5 N1's, exchange barley, 37 months, Kushim's final account'. It is one of the best-known of the earliest written documents.

Proto-cuneiform is the earliest stage of cuneiform writing, used for bookkeeping in southern Mesopotamia. It records numbers in several counting systems (shown in the transliteration as signs N01, N14, N34 and so on) together with signs for goods, offices and places. It does not yet write full sentences, so the English is an interpretation of the entries rather than a translation of connected language.

The sections follow the faces and columns of the tablet. The transliteration and the English are CDLI's, line by line with the same line numbers.
translator_notes: Transliteration: CDLI ATF (proto-cuneiform). Numerals are written as counts of numeral signs, e.g. 4(N14) = four N14 signs; ~a, ~b mark sign variants; [ ] broken, # damaged; sz is shown as š.
English: CDLI's line-by-line translation (#tr.en lines of the ATF).
CDLI notes: obverse, line 1: ca. 135,000 liters
